Tom / Lauren — technical detail below; I'll keep it compact and call out the key SLAs.

1) Backup types and cadence
- Snapshots (daily full snapshots of model state + customer metadata): created nightly at 02:00 UTC; retained in primary region for 90 days by default (configurable per-account).
- Object-store backups (incremental blobs of customer data, stored in S3 buckets replicated cross-region for DR): incremental every 4 hours, retention default 180 days.
- KV-cache checkpoints / ephemeral caches: checkpointed every 30 minutes and treated as short-lived (7 days) unless pinned for debugging.

2) Deletion flow when customer issues an API delete request
- Live data: immediate logical deletion from primary stores; propagation to search/index services is near-real-time (<1 minute).
- Backup/replica marking: within 24 hours of delete request, backups that contain the deleted object are flagged for erasure during the next scheduled sweep job.
- Sweep windows: we run a nightly backup-sweep job that rehydrates index-maps and schedules object-level deletion for flagged blobs. The actual object erasure completes within the next 3 nightly sweep runs (so up to ~72 hours from flagging) for primary-region backups.
- Cross-region replicas: deletion jobs are queued for each replica and typically apply within 48–120 hours depending on cross-region replication lag and compliance-oriented staggered jobs to avoid availability impact.

3) Snapshots vs object blobs nuance
- Immutable snapshot images are versioned; we do not mutate historical snapshot files. Instead, snapshots that reference objects with deletions are rewritten on sweep to remove references and then the old snapshot is tombstoned and garbage-collected per the schedule above. Practical implication: snapshot rewrite + GC can add additional hours compared to object-blob erasure.

4) Legal hold and retention suspension
- If Medsys places a legal hold (via support/legal request referencing account + hold id), we will suspend deletion propagation for all flagged items for the duration of the hold. Holds must include: account id, hold id, start date, expected end date (or indefinite).
- Holds are visible in the console and in the audit log. Holds are applied within 4 hours of request processing.

5) Audit evidence & certificates
- We can provide: per-object deletion events (log lines), sweep-run reports (which list objects removed per run), and a signed attestation PDF for compliance reviews.
- For high-assurance needs, we can produce a timeline bundle (JSON) showing delete request id -> flagged backups -> sweep-run ids -> final GC confirmation.

6) Exceptions & SLA notes
- Emergency/accelerated purge: for customers under a support plan, we can request an expedited erase that attempts to accelerate GC; typical turn time: 24–96 hours depending on object size and replication.
- If an account has offsite/air-gapped private backups (on-prem), erasure timelines depend on the customer's control plane process; Redwood provides the signal but the physical erase is coordinated with the customer.

I'll attach a CSV matrix that maps retention defaults to erase windows per backup type. If you want tighter SLAs we can propose shorter retention/accelerated purge add-ons.

- Aditya

Tom — a few compliance points from legal: 

- Our standard deletion attestation covers the steps Aditya outlined and includes timestamps and operator IDs for sweep-run confirmations. That attestation is suitable for SOC reviews in most cases.
- For regulatory holds (e.g., e-discovery), Medsys should supply a signed hold notice with scope. Once received we will lock the relevant object IDs and log the hold.
- Note on jurisdictional constraints: if Medsys data is covered by a country-level requirement to retain copies (rare), Redwood will not override a lawful retention order. We will, however, work with you on the narrowest scope.
